_comment: Mutation testing on the trust-critical modules (issue #187, part of #178). Diff-coverage proves changed lines EXECUTE; mutation testing proves the tests would CATCH a bug. Scope is deliberately limited to the highest-stakes pure logic: trust derivations (app/trust), the manual-entry dedup matcher (app/server/listings/dedup.ts), and the write rate limiter (app/server/rate-limit). ignoreStatic is ON (AUB-201): static mutants — mutations in module-level initialization, where perTest coverage can't apply so EACH ONE re-runs the whole suite — were, per Stryker's own MutantTestPlanner warning on the CI run that prompted this, 60 mutants (13%) consuming an estimated ~92% of the runtime (the local re-measure below counted 56 static of 454 generated); ignoring them cut the run from tens of minutes to ~5m22s. TRADE-OFF: static mutants are now UNSCORED, so this gate no longer exercises module-level constants (e.g. RECENT_INCIDENT_WINDOW_DAYS, DEFAULT_STALENESS_MONTHS, DEFAULT_WRITE_RATE_LIMIT, the CLAIM_ATTRIBUTE_* maps). The highest-stakes ones stay pinned by ordinary hardcoded-literal tests that Stryker never ran for them anyway: the 90-day incident window (trust-model.invariant.test.ts), the rate-limit config (rate-limit/index.test.ts toEqual({limit:50,windowMs:60_000})), and staleness-window growth (summary.test.ts's literal 7-month check); a shrink of DEFAULT_STALENESS_MONTHS to 3-5 is the one unpinned direction, accepted because it fails SAFE (flags staleness earlier, never later). Ignored static mutants leave the score's denominator, so the baseline was RE-MEASURED with ignoreStatic on: total mutation score 84.62% across 403 runtime mutants (summary 97.04, browse-glance 96.77, browse-card-format 95.24, rate-limit 84.21, dedup 71.88, incident-recency 62.50 — the last dragged down by Zod error-message string literals and TZ paths the DB-free suite can't fairly kill). thresholds.break is 84 (rounded DOWN from 84.62) so it PASSES today on a green main and can be ratcheted up as tests improve — it is intentionally NOT set above the measured score, which would false-fail a green main. To raise the floor, add tests that kill surviving mutants (see reports/mutation/mutation.html) and bump break. CURRENT BASELINE (supersedes the 84.62%/403 figures above, which predate the TypeScript 7 break and are kept only as history): measured 95.40% across 413 scored mutants, 394 killed, 19 surviving, 0 without coverage. thresholds.break is 93, NOT 95. Rounding straight down from 95.40 would leave 1 mutant of slack (95% of 413 needs 393 killed), which guarantees a false-failure on the next unrelated change; 93 needs 385 and leaves 9. That gap is deliberate drift room, not headroom to spend — the gate only fires on PRs touching these paths, so a dependency bump can shift outcomes unmeasured and the next trust PR absorbs it. THE 19 SURVIVORS ARE DOCUMENTED, NOT IGNORED. Provably equivalent: dedup.ts:66/:68 (`+` quantifiers made unobservable by the trailing trim/collapse — 200k-string fuzz, 0 differing outputs); incident-recency.ts:89/:90 (month and date halves of the round-trip overflow check are individually redundant — all 100,000,000 YYYY-MM-DD inputs brute-forced, no input fires only one; the year half DOES have 36,524 solo cases and is now killed); browse-glance.ts:156/:157 (non-taxonomy defaults are filtered back to [] by normalizeAttributes); incident-recency.ts:278 x4 (guard only changes the answer when `now` predates 1970-04-01). Unkillable in this environment: incident-recency.ts:131 x5 — observable only on a negative-offset runtime TZ, and the file's TZ block skipIf's itself under worker threads while Stryker's vitest-runner hard-codes the threads pool (same root cause as the #144 note). Judgment calls left unpinned: :142 padStart (years < 1000 are unreachable), :179/:227 (`day !== null` -> true changes no accept/reject outcome), :303 (`>` vs `>=` is a genuinely unspecified tie-break between same-day incidents). Before raising break again, read that list — several of these cannot be killed without padding. The high/low bands are report colouring only (break is the sole failure point); they are set to 95/85 so they still bracket break=93 meaningfully rather than sitting below it, where every passing run would render as high.
tsconfigFile_comment: AUB-258 workaround, NOT a normal setting. This points at a file that does not exist ON PURPOSE. TypeScript 7 (PR #320) removed ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson, which @stryker-mutator/core still calls from TSConfigPreprocessor, so the job crashed before running a single mutant. NO released Stryker fixes this: 10.0.0 (published 2026-08-14) carries the identical call at ts-config-preprocessor.js:46, and pinning TypeScript back would revert #320 repo-wide. That preprocessor exists only to rewrite paths that would escape the sandbox, and it skips the removed API entirely when the tsconfig is not found in the project, so an unresolvable path sidesteps the crash. PRECONDITION, and it is the whole reason this is safe: tsconfig.json here uses NEITHER `extends` NOR `references`, AND its include/exclude/files entries all resolve inside the repo root. The preprocessor rewrites all five, so if any of them ever points outside the repo, revisit this. Verified on this branch: 2 TypeErrors before, 0 after; full run exit 0, mutation score 84.50 vs break 84 (349 killed of 413 scored). REMOVE THIS and restore the default tsconfigFile once Stryker ships a TypeScript 7-compatible release.
